papers.title_en: QuantumQUBO Agent: Automating Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) Formulation Generation from Natural Language
papers.authors: Niloy Kumar Mondal, Md Rizwan Parvez
papers.evidence: 从自然语言自动生成QUBO组合优化建模的多智能体框架
papers.tldr: 二次无约束二值优化（QUBO）是组合优化与量子求解的重要建模形式，但从自然语言问题描述自动生成正确QUBO仍依赖专家、耗时且易错。为此，作者提出端到端多智能体框架，自动识别变量、约束、目标与罚项并生成QUBO公式。该框架在QUBOBench上取得68%准确率，比单次直接调用基线提升22%。消融显示迭代自修复最关键，代码与基准已开源。
papers.abstract_en: Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) is a central formulation for combinatorial optimization and has gained increasing attention due to its compatibility with quantum, hybrid quantum-classical, and quantum-inspired solvers. However, translating natural-language problem descriptions into correct QUBO formulations remains difficult, requiring the identification of binary variables, constraints, objective functions, penalty terms, and suitable penalty weights. This process is time-consuming and often demands substantial domain expertise. To address this challenge, we propose an end-to-end multi-agent framework that automatically generates QUBO formulations from natural-language problem descriptions, supported by structured or unstructured test cases. To evaluate its performance, We also introduce QUBOBench, a benchmark containing 100 combinatorial optimization problems across 12 application domains, curated from peer-reviewed literature, competitions, and canonical NP-hard problems. Experimental results show that our framework achieves 68% accuracy on QUBOBench, outperforming a direct single-call baseline by 22%. Further analysis identifies iterative self-repair as the most important component contributing to improved performance. The data and code are open-sourced at https://quitttcat.github.io/QuantumQUBOAgent.

papers.title_en: MAPLE: Memory-Augmented Planning with Language and Evolution
papers.authors: Kesheng Chen, Yamin Hu, Wenjian Luo
papers.evidence: 基于LLM的优化智能体通过连续自然语言请求维护运筹优化模型
papers.tldr: 业务人员懂自身约束却缺乏运筹优化专长，LLM 智能体虽能把自然语言需求转成可执行的优化模型，但现实运营中需求、资源与目标不断变化，孤立的单次请求难以在保留既有决策的同时快速适配。MAPLE 将语言驱动的问题构建与数学规划、进化搜索结合，并记忆优化程序、已接受方案、历史更新与候选解。在 NLDO 基准的 15 条轨迹、180 次更新上全部完成，在线标量质量达 0.951，Pareto 超体积比 0.875。这表维护可执行状态可提升更新有效性，并跨大幅修订保留有用搜索信息。
papers.abstract_en: Domain practitioners understand their business constraints but may lack operations-research expertise or dedicated support. LLM-based optimization agents translate natural-language requirements into models or solver programs that established optimization tools can execute. This progress makes optimization more accessible, but real-world operations are dynamic: changing demand, resources, and priorities require updates to data, constraints, and objectives. Methods centered on isolated requests offer limited support for rapid adaptation that preserves earlier decisions and reuses useful search results. We introduce MAPLE (Memory-Augmented Planning with Language and Evolution), an agent for maintaining optimization problems through successive natural-language requests. MAPLE combines language-based problem construction with mathematical programming and evolutionary search. It retains the optimization program, accepted plans, earlier updates, and candidate solutions for subsequent requests. We introduce NLDO, a benchmark of 15 trajectories and 180 updates spanning selection, scheduling, rostering, routing, and cloud-resource placement. In the main evaluation, MAPLE completes all trajectories and achieves online scalar quality of 0.951 and a Pareto hypervolume ratio of 0.875. Controlled comparisons further show that maintaining executable state improves update validity and can preserve useful search information across substantial revisions.

papers.title_en: GenOR-Twin: A Semantic Middleware for Integrating Operational Discourse with Mathematical Optimization
papers.authors: Rahimeh Neamatian Monemi, Shahin Gelareh, Lubin Cui, Nelson Maculan
papers.evidence: LLM将运营日志转译为数学约束
papers.tldr: GenOR-Twin面向非结构化运行日志与严格数学优化之间的翻译鸿沟，将大语言模型定位为语义翻译器而非直接求解器，以保留精确组合方法的可行性保证。它通过动态约束注入把定性中断事件实时转为形式化约束，并借助双向耦合让运行观测更新虚拟模型、优化决策回写知识图谱。系统还按可用松弛量自适应选择轻量修复或全量重优化，并在六个优化域验证了泛化能力。
papers.abstract_en: We introduce GenOR-Twin, a neuro-symbolic framework that bridges the translation gap between unstructured operational logs and rigorous mathematical optimization. Our architecture uniquely positions Large Language Models as semantic translators rather than direct solvers, ensuring that the system retains the feasibility guarantees of exact combinatorial methods. { \color{red}We design a dynamic constraint injection mechanism (the runtime translation of qualitative disruption events into formal mathematical constraints) that allows the system to structurally modify the optimization problem's feasibility region in real-time based on qualitative human inputs. The resulting bidirectional coupling---where operational observations update the virtual model state and optimized decisions are reflected back into the Knowledge Graph---satisfies the synchronization requirement of a proper Digital Twin. The framework features an adaptive decision policy} that automatically selects between low-complexity schedule repair and full re-optimization by analyzing the available system slack. Finally, we demonstrate the generalization of this approach across six distinct optimization domains, {\color{red}turning static models into resilient systems that adapt to the operational uncertainty and variability of real-world environments.}

papers.title_en: SAILOR: Solver-Assisted Interactive LLM-based Optimization Recovery
papers.authors: Shaghayegh Sadeghi, Stephen L. Smith, David C. Del Rey Fern'andez
papers.evidence: 用LLM将自然语言优化问题转为求解器模型并恢复缺失数值
papers.tldr: 自然语言描述的优化问题常缺失求解器所需的数值信息，如成本、容量、需求、边界和惩罚项，LLM 转代码时若值缺失只能停止或猜测。SAILOR 检测这些无依据的数值选择，向用户提出针对性追问，并在返回解前更新优化模型；追问按不确定性和求解器估计的缺失值对当前模型影响排序。在七个掩码基准的 1,723 个实例上，目标值完全一致率为 27.0%–87.6%，平均每实例提问 1.4–5.7 次，验证了受控分支揭示反馈下的可行性。
papers.abstract_en: Natural-language descriptions of optimization problems may be incomplete or vague about numerical information that a solver requires, including costs, capacities, demands, bounds, and penalties. A language model can translate the description into code, but when a required value is absent it must either stop or guess. We present SAILOR, a proof-of-concept system that detects such unsupported numerical choices, asks the user targeted follow-up questions, and updates the optimization model before returning a solution. Questions are prioritized using uncertainty and solver-derived estimates of how strongly each missing value affects the current model. We evaluate the pipeline on 1,723 instances from seven masked benchmarks using an idealized simulator that returns ground-truth values. Exact objective-value agreement ranges from 27.0% to 87.6% across datasets, with 1.4--5.7 questions per instance on average. These results establish feasibility under controlled branch-and-reveal feedback; they do not measure performance with human users or general structural model repair. Code is available at: https://github.com/sshaghayeghs/SAILOR.

papers.title_en: little m: An AI Agent for Industrial Process Optimization
papers.authors: Yongchao Ye, Xinyu He, Dutliff Boshoff, Way Kuo, Lishuai Li
papers.evidence: AI智能体从自然语言规格辅助构建数学优化模型
papers.tldr: 工业过程优化需要数学优化模型，但从杂乱规范、文本与工艺图中建模，对通用LLM仍很困难，易产生无效约束。本文提出AI智能体little m，融合领域知识库与LLM交互，将真实优化问题形式化为数学模型。同时发布IPC-Bench，包含50个文本与流程图联合推理场景。自动结构评估和双盲人工评测表明，little m显著优于SOTA LLM，能生成语义正确模型，推动工业过程控制建模自动化。
papers.abstract_en: Manufacturing consumes one third of global energy and still has significant room for improvement in terms of energy efficiency. Optimal process control is essential for this purpose. However, synthesizing mathematical optimization models from messy, real-world industrial specifications requires bridging unstructured natural language and spatial diagrams with rigorous mathematical syntax. This poses a profound challenge for general-purpose Large Language Models (LLMs), which may introduce invalid constraints when tasked with modeling continuous multi-physics dynamics. To address this, we introduce little m, an AI agent designed to assist the formulation of industrial process control models. Combining a domain-specific knowledge repository with LLM-driven interaction, the proposed framework formulates real-world optimization problems as mathematical models. For systematic evaluation, we introduce the Industrial Process Control Benchmark (IPC-Bench), a novel multimodal dataset of 50 canonical scenarios requiring joint reasoning over text and process diagrams. Through comprehensive automated structural assessments and double-blind human evaluation, little m substantially outperforms state-of-the-art LLMs, generating semantically correct models. These evaluations assess formulation quality rather than solver feasibility, formal physical validity, or closed-loop industrial performance. The implementation of little m and the IPC-Bench dataset are available at https://github.com/yeyongchao/process-modeling-benchmark.
